title: pixel game problems - scaling in browser
author: Shnatrix
selftext:
Hi Guys,

I started the task of making what I thought was a simple pixel game in browser, now everything was running swimmingly till I tried to add in a pixel style font.... Then I think I've burnt days if not weeks of trying to debug it with codex, replit, antigravity AND claude. No one's been able to get it right.

And when AI can't... hopefully we can.

Please see screenshots of what I'm dealing with

Essentially pixels is math - and I've changed it to bitmap text, and that is okay provided it stays at a certain size OR I bake in the text to the image. I am beginning to wonder in modern builds is that just the best way to do it, everything is just png files, and you don't have any text? 

I was wondering if anyone else is building something similar and could help me or if simply browser is just not the way to go.

So I either have massive compression and it's poop or I have smudgy text because it's not rendering at pixel perfect. HELP! :)

comments.author: whatsbetweenatoms
comments.body:
Pixel fonts don't scale, they have an original "native" size and that's it. The only scaling you can do, is doubling the size (or any whole number multiple of original size) any other scaling in-between that will look like garbage and fractional pixel placement will also cause it to fail. This is why most pixel art games don't actually use pixel fonts. And yes bitmap font is most crisp, but again, you can't scale it. You have to pre-render every size, not fun. I'd highly recommend using a normal font that is square-ish rather than a pixel font.


Look at Celeste amazing pixel art game, normal vector fonts. Why? Because its easier to scale on various devices / platforms. Pixel fonts are a nightmare.

replies.author: Shnatrix
replies.body: Just started changing things over to vector. God damn if I just asked a week ago could have saved a lot of time and headache

replies.author: RealAstropulse
replies.body: You can also convert bitmap fonts to vector fonts and scale them to any resolution. It looks to me like the scaling method used here was the issue. No doubt the ai messed it up and was doing weird stuff.

replies.author: whatsbetweenatoms
replies.body: In my experience this doesn't work in practice, it works for scaling up (somewhat), but you will have the same issues at small sizes, which is the whole point of using a pixel font. This isn't an "ai problem" its a "pixel fonts have always been an issue, even before ai" problem. I'm interested in your process though. As I just went through this on two games and ultimately decided that pixel fonts aren't worth the effort. The best I was able to achieve was by rendering text larger res than its supposed to be, then downscaling it.

replies.author: RealAstropulse
replies.body: Oh yeah, if you're trying to scale pixel fonts below their intended resolution there is no way to do it. You have to be smart about your font sizes and have several sizes picked out for different situations.

replies.author: Shnatrix
replies.body: Well it's still trying to fix it - I just asked it to get rid of all the font alterations and still can't get it to land for some reason. Another day down
